note: Every measure below is count-free: it does not require knowing which vertebra is which. Level names cannot be assigned from a spine-limited field of view, because the same bone is called a sacralised L5 or a lumbarised S1 depending only on where the count starts.

panels.section: Who is in this dataset
panels.section_note: Every case comes from CT colonography -- a colorectal cancer SCREENING examination. The age floor visible in the data is the screening guideline showing through, not a choice made here. So this is an asymptomatic screening population rather than a surgical or back-pain series: the spinopelvic measures below sit closer to a reference range than a clinical cohort would, and the transitional variants were found incidentally.
panels.title: Age, by sex
panels.subtitle: a screening population: the lower bound is the guideline, not a filter
panels.caption: Median 58 years in women and 59 in men. Nothing below the screening age threshold appears because nothing below it was scanned.

panels.section: Who is in this dataset
panels.title: Sex
panels.subtitle: as recorded in the source metadata
panels.caption: Recorded in the source collection, not inferred from the images. Cases with no recorded value are shown rather than dropped.

panels.section: Who is in this dataset
panels.title: How each record was assembled
panels.subtitle: spine and pelvic labels do not always land on the same acquisition
panels.caption: Each patient was scanned prone and supine. Where both label sets landed on one acquisition the record is fused; otherwise the two are exported separately, which is why a patient can appear as more than one record.

panels.section: Who is in this dataset
panels.title: Transitional label carried by the source
panels.subtitle: from the source collections, not adjudicated here
panels.xlabel: Transitional label carried by the source
panels.caption: These are the labels the source collections carried. They are shown as they arrived, and are not all expert-adjudicated -- which is exactly why the measures on this page are count-free and do not depend on them.

panels.section: Anatomy of the transition
panels.title: Non-rib-bearing vertebrae
panels.subtitle: counted BETWEEN the lowest rib and the sacrum — an interval, not a level
panels.caption: Five is typical. Four and six are where transitional anatomy sits — and which of the two you see does not tell you what to call it.

panels.section: Anatomy of the transition
panels.title: Lowest rib length, as a fraction of the rib above
panels.subtitle: hypoplastic twelfth ribs form their own population
panels.caption: Two modes, near 0.68 and near 0.32 — not one distribution with a tail. That shape is what a discrete developmental variant looks like. The curve is a kernel density estimate; the ticks beneath it are the cases themselves, thinned.

panels.section: Anatomy of the transition
panels.title: Lowest disc gap ÷ the disc above it
panels.subtitle: dimensionless, so it compares across patients
panels.caption: A rudimentary lowest disc runs low. Values near zero also arise from fusion of any cause — congenital, surgical or bridging osteophyte — which is why this measure alone cannot say why a gap closed.

panels.section: Anatomy of the transition
panels.title: How far the lowest lumbar reaches, and how close it comes to the ala
panels.subtitle: one point per side — the asymmetry is the phenotype
panels.caption: Castellvi grades on a process that approaches, articulates with, or fuses to the sacral ala. Span and gap carry most of that without naming the level.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Pelvic incidence
panels.subtitle: position-independent: identical standing, seated and supine
panels.caption: A morphological property of the pelvis rather than a posture, which is why it needs no caveat on a supine CT, and why it sets how much lordosis a given spine requires.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Sacral slope
panels.subtitle: postural, reported supine
panels.caption: The sacral plate measured against the horizontal.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Pelvic tilt
panels.subtitle: postural, reported supine
panels.caption: Pelvic incidence less sacral slope. It rises as a pelvis retroverts to compensate for lost lordosis.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Lumbar lordosis, supine
panels.subtitle: supine sits about 4.6 degrees below standing; it is SEATED that collapses
panels.caption: Measured only where the arc reaches the top of the lumbar segment. A field of view that clips the upper lumbar spine returns a smaller angle than the patient actually has, and that error would land in the mismatch below.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: PI-LL mismatch
panels.subtitle: the decision-maker: beyond about 10 degrees predicts residual pain after fusion
panels.caption: Centred near zero across an unoperated cohort, which is the check that the two angles were measured independently and still agree.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Iliac crest above the L4-5 disc
panels.subtitle: the lateral corridor: positive means the crest obstructs a lateral approach
panels.caption: The dashed line is the published 12 mm cutoff, above which subsidence risk rises after oblique lateral fusion at that level.
panels.xlabel: Iliac crest above the L4-5 disc (mm)

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Lowest rib to iliac crest
panels.subtitle: the other boundary of the same corridor
panels.caption: This is where the rib work becomes operative: a hypoplastic or absent twelfth rib moves the upper limit of the working window.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Narrowest lumbar pedicle
panels.subtitle: selects screw diameter, and is itself a phenotype
panels.caption: Measured at the isthmus, per side, taking the narrower of the two.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Does the lumbar spine match the pelvis it sits on?
panels.subtitle: one point per case; the diagonal is a perfect match
panels.caption: Points below the diagonal have less lordosis than their pelvis calls for. The cloud sits ON the line, which is what an unoperated cohort should do and is the strongest evidence these two angles were measured independently.

panels.section: Spinopelvic alignment and the surgical corridor
panels.title: Pelvic incidence by sex
panels.subtitle: reported because the cohort carries age and sex, not because it separates
panels.caption: Median 55.1 degrees in women against 54.7 in men, a difference of 0.4. Pelvic dimorphism is strong in shape -- subpubic angle, inlet proportions, the sciatic notch -- and pelvic incidence is not one of those measures, so a null here agrees with the series that report no sex difference in it.

panels.section: Pelvic shape, by sex
panels.title: Pelvic width, across the iliac crests
panels.subtitle: the widest span of the bony pelvis
panels.xlabel: Pelvic width, across the iliac crests (mm)
panels.caption: The measurement most people mean by pelvic width. Men are wider in absolute terms because men are larger overall; the female pelvis is wider relative to its size, and that shows in shape measures rather than in this one. Median 272 mm in women against 283 mm in men, a difference of 10 mm.
panels.section_note: Pelvic incidence -- the angle above -- does not separate by sex, and several published series agree that it does not. Sexual dimorphism in the pelvis is a matter of SHAPE: how wide it is, how round the inlet is, how the sacrum is proportioned. Those are measured here, drawn as two overlaid distributions so the separation is visible rather than asserted, and each caption gives both medians and the gap between them.

panels.section: Pelvic shape, by sex
panels.title: Width across the hip joints
panels.subtitle: centre to centre between the femoral heads
panels.caption: Measured from the part of the femur in contact with the acetabulum. The femur labels run 61-109 mm from head to shaft, so a whole-label centroid sits down the shaft and read 18 mm too wide before this was corrected. Median 166 mm in women against 167 mm in men, a difference of 2 mm.

panels.section: How the lumbar spine changes as it descends
panels.title: The spinal canal widens as it descends
panels.subtitle: transverse diameter, level by level
panels.caption: Published series run from about 22 mm at L1 to 26.5 at L5, and that is the gradient here. The canal keeps widening below the end of the cord, where it carries only the cauda equina. Median 23.9 to 30.0mm across 5 levels.
panels.section_note: Almost every dimension of a lumbar vertebra grows from L1 downward, because each level carries everything above it. That makes the gradient a stronger check than any single measurement: it either reproduces the published trend or it does not. Two of the four measured here reproduce and are shown; anterior body height and the wedge ratio do not, and are not.

panels.section: How the lumbar spine changes as it descends
panels.title: Vertebral bodies broaden under load
panels.subtitle: superior endplate, side to side
panels.caption: About 41.8 mm at L1 rising to 50.7 at L5 in published series; measured here at 43.9, 45.8, 48.6 and 51.3. L5 is omitted: it reads 67.5 mm, which is not a wide L5 but the body/process separation failing, since the L5 transverse processes arise close enough to the body to survive the cut that isolates it. Median 43.9 to 51.3mm across 4 levels.
